artists.biography:
Supergrass was an English alternative rock band from Oxford. The band consisted of brothers Gaz (guitar and lead vocals) and Rob Coombes (keyboards), Mick Quinn (bass and backing vocals) and Danny Goffey (drums and backing vocals).
Gaz Coombes, Mick Quinn and Danny Goffey formed Supergrass in 1993 in Oxford with Gaz's brother Rob Coombes officially joining the band in 2002. The band signed to Parlophone records in 1994 and produced I Should Coco (1995), the biggest selling début album for the label since the Beatles' Please Please Me. Their first album's fourth single Alright was a huge international hit that established the band's reputation. Since then the band have released five albums: In It for the Money (1997), Supergrass (1999), Life on Other Planets (2002), Road to Rouen (2005) and Diamond Hoo Ha (2008), as well as a decade-ending compilation called Supergrass is 10 (2004).

perplexity.description:
I Should Coco is the debut studio album by British rock band Supergrass, released in May 1995 through Parlophone. Characterized by its energetic blend of Britpop, punk, ska, and psychedelic influences, the album captures the youthful exuberance of the band, who were still teenagers at the time of recording. Produced by Sam Williams and recorded at Sawmills Studios in Cornwall, the album features 13 tracks, including early singles like "Caught by the Fuzz," "Mansize Rooster," and the breakout hit "Alright." The music is marked by catchy melodies, driving guitar riffs, and playful lyrics, earning it the reputation as "the sound of adolescence" during the height of the Britpop era.

As Supergrass's first full-length release, I Should Coco established the band as a major force in British rock. It reached number one on the UK Albums Chart and achieved platinum status, selling over a million copies worldwide and more than 500,000 in the UK alone. The album was widely praised for its originality and vitality, with critics highlighting its eclectic style and the band's raw energy. It remains a landmark debut in the Britpop movement and a defining moment in Supergrass's discography.
